input.rationale: Drift: the file adds one column, network_status, at the end (position 15). Its name is usable, it is filled in all 5 rows, and every value is "IN" (shape AA). Nothing else changed: same columns, same order, same types. The change looks deliberate (a clean, consistent code column), not a vendor mistake, so I added it to the contract as an optional column: type string, allowed: [IN], phi: false (the profile labels it non-PHI; it is a network status, not a person identifier). It is not required, so files without it are not rejected. Loosening: none reported by validate_contract. Note for review: allowed: [IN] is taken from the single observed value; if the vendor later sends other values (e.g. OUT), those rows will be quarantined until the list is widened by a person. Also flagged, not changed (rule 2 keeps existing columns as they are): the profile labels claim_line_id, claim_id, member_id and service_date as phi: true, but the current contract has them without phi. Someone should decide whether to set phi on them. Dry run: 5 accepted, 0 rejected. Version bumped 1 -> 2.

content.text:
The file added one new column, `network_status`, at the end. Its values are all "IN" in all 5 rows, and nothing else changed, so this looks like a deliberate vendor addition rather than a mistake.

I added it to the contract as an optional string column with `allowed: [IN]` and `phi: false`, and bumped the version from 1 to 2. The validator reported no loosening. Dry run: 5 accepted, 0 rejected. Candidate `7cf96e9abc75a4f7` is submitted for review.

Two things for the reviewer. The `allowed: [IN]` list comes from a single observed value, so a future "OUT" would be quarantined until someone widens it. The profile also labels `claim_line_id`, `claim_id`, `member_id` and `service_date` as PHI, but the current contract doesn't mark them. I left those alone because drift mode keeps existing columns' rules as they are, but someone should decide whether to set `phi` on them.
